title_en: China Cinda Asset Management Corporation Xi'an Office v. Shaanxi Provincial Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import and Export Corporation Xi'an Transit Cold Storage and Shaanxi Provincial Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import and Export Corporation — dispute over a loan guarantee contract
ruling_gist_en: According to the provisions of Article 31 of the Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, when real estate is transferred or mortgaged, the ownership of the house and the land use right within the area occupied by the house shall be transferred or mortgaged simultaneously. The Administrative Measures for the Registration of Urban House Ownership also stipulate: 'The registration of house ownership shall follow the principle of consistency between the owner of the house and the holder of the land use right within the area occupied by the house.' Accordingly, the real estate transferor has the obligation to transfer the land use right within the area occupied by the sold house to the transferee, and the transferee has the right to demand that the land use right within the area occupied by the purchased house be transferred to the transferee. Before the completion of the registration of the change of land use right, the transferor is the registered nominal right holder, but if the transferee is the substantive right holder, the transferee may request that the land use right be changed to the transferee's name.

full_text_en:
China Cinda Asset Management Corporation, Xi'an Office v.

Shaanxi Provincial Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import & Export Corporation, Xi'an Transit Cold Storage,

and Shaanxi Provincial Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import & Export Corporation

— Dispute over loan guarantee contract

Ruling Summary

In accordance with Article 31 of the Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the People's Republic of China, when real estate is transferred or mortgaged, the ownership of the building and the land use rights within the building's footprint shall be transferred or mortgaged simultaneously. The Measures for the Administration of Urban Building Ownership Registration also provide that: "Registration of building ownership shall follow the principle of consistency between the ownership of the building and the land use rights within the building's footprint." Accordingly, the transferor of a building has the obligation to transfer the land use rights within the footprint of the sold building to the transferee, and the transferee has the right to request that the land use rights within the footprint of the purchased building be transferred to itself. Before the completion of the modification registration of the land use rights, the transferor is the nominal rights holder on the register, but if the transferee is the substantive rights holder, it may request that the land use rights be modified and registered under its own name.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Judgment

(2007) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 222

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Cinda Asset Management Corporation, Xi'an Office, domiciled at: No. 15 Nan Da Jie, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Responsible Person: Li Yuejin, General Manager of the Office.

Agent ad litem: Yang Jinming, lawyer of Beijing Zhongkai Law Firm, Xi'an Branch.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Shaanxi Provincial Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import & Export Corporation, Xi'an Transit Cold Storage, domiciled at: Office Building of Xi'an Transit Cold Storage, Maqizhai Road, Xinjiamiao, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Meng Jinming, Director of the Cold Storage.

Agent ad litem: Hu Xiping, lawyer of Beijing Shixianzhe Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Fan Bilian, lawyer of Beijing Shixianzhe Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Shaanxi Provincial Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import & Export Corporation, domiciled at: Room 301, Office Building of Xi'an Transit Cold Storage, Maqizhai Road, Xinjiamiao, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Zhao Lei, General Manager of the Corporation.

Agent ad litem: Wei Bo, Deputy General Manager of the Corporation.

In the dispute over the loan guarantee contract between the appellant China Cinda Asset Management Corporation, Xi'an Office (hereinafter referred to as Cinda Xi'an Office) and the appellee Shaanxi Provincial Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import & Export Corporation, Xi'an Transit Cold Storage (hereinafter referred to as Transit Cold Storage), and the defendant at first instance Shaanxi Provincial Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import & Export Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Cereals and Oils Company), the Shaanxi High People's Court rendered the Civil Judgment (2007) Shan Min Er Chu Zi No. 2 on July 8, 2007. Cinda Xi'an Office, dissatisfied with the judgment, appealed to this Court. This Court, in accordance with the law, formed a collegial panel composed of Judge Jin Jianfeng as the presiding judge, and acting judges Yin Yuan and Pan Yongfeng to hear the case, with Zhao Suijun as the court clerk. The case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts after trial:

On March 16, 2003, the Cereals and Oils Company and the Shaanxi Branch of the Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as BOC Shaanxi Branch) entered into a "Renminbi Loan Contract" numbered 2003 Shan Zhong Ying Jie Zi No. 022, agreeing that the Cereals and Oils Company would borrow RMB 25.6 million from BOC Shaanxi Branch, with a loan term of 12 months, the loan purpose being "new loan to repay old loan" (jixin huanjiu), and the loan interest rate being 5.31% per annum, guaranteed by a mortgage provided by the Transit Cold Storage. If the Cereals and Oils Company failed to repay the loan within the agreed term, overdue portion would accrue interest at 2.1 ten-thousandths per day. Overdue interest rates would be adjusted in stages when the interest rate is adjusted. On the same day, the Transit Cold Storage and BOC Shaanxi Branch entered into a "Mortgage Contract" numbered 2003 Shan Zhong Ying Di Zi No. 022, under which the Transit Cold Storage used its 44.46 mu of land use rights, valued at RMB 41.0655 million, as mortgage security for the Cereals and Oils Company's loan of RMB 25.6 million. Article 2 of the mortgage contract stipulated that if both parties to the loan contract agreed to modify the contract terms, except for increasing the loan amount, the consent of the mortgagor would not be required, and the mortgagor should bear the security liability in accordance with the modified scope of the creditor's rights. If the parties to the loan contract increased the loan amount without the mortgagor's consent, the mortgagor would still bear the security liability within the original loan amount. If the mortgagee assigned the creditor's rights under the loan contract to a third party, the mortgaged property would continue to secure the debt, and such creditor's rights would be satisfied with priority. On March 17, 2003, BOC Shaanxi Branch disbursed RMB 25.6 million to the Cereals and Oils Company, and the Cereals and Oils Company repaid the old loan with BOC Shaanxi Branch. On March 28, 2003, the Xi'an Municipal Bureau of Land Resources and Housing Administration issued a reply to the Transit Cold Storage's letter regarding consent to continue using land and above-ground buildings for loan mortgage. The reply stated: "We have received the 'Letter on Consent to Continue Using Land and Above-ground Buildings for Loan Mortgage' submitted by your unit, along with the Mortgage Contract numbered 2003 Shan Zhong Ying Di Zi No. 022 signed between your unit and the Bank of China, Shaanxi Branch, and the Renminbi Loan Contract numbered 2003 Shan Zhong Ying Jie Zi No. 022 signed between Shaanxi Provincial Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import & Export Corporation and the Bank of China, Shaanxi Branch, and other attachments. According to the Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the People's Republic of China and the 'Measures for the Administration of Urban Real Estate Mortgage' of the Ministry of Construction, after study, it is approved that your unit may set a mortgage on the land use rights located at Xinjiamiao, Weiyang District, Xi'an City, with the Bank of China, Shaanxi Branch, to guarantee Shaanxi Provincial Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs Import & Export Corporation's loan of RMB 25.6 million, with a mortgage term of 12 months from the date of registration. The mortgage certificates are the State-Owned Land Use Certificates Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979 and Xi Wei Guo Yong (2001) Zi No. 299. According to relevant regulations, during the mortgage period, without the consent of the mortgagee, the ownership of the land use rights and the above-ground buildings and fixtures shall not be transferred."

On June 25, 2004, BOC Shaanxi Branch and Cinda Xi'an Office entered into a "Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement," under which BOC Shaanxi Branch transferred to Cinda Xi'an Office the creditor's rights of RMB 25.6 million and ancillary rights against the Cereals and Oils Company. On November 10, 2004, BOC Shaanxi Branch and Cinda Xi'an Office published a "Creditor's Rights Transfer and Collection Announcement" in the "Shaanxi Daily," notifying the Cereals and Oils Company of the transfer of creditor's rights, and simultaneously, the assignee Cinda Xi'an Office asserted its rights against the Cereals and Oils Company. On June 18, 2006, Cinda Xi'an Office again published an announcement in the "Shaanxi Daily" asserting its rights against the Cereals and Oils Company.

The court of first instance additionally found that among the 44.466 mu of state-owned allocated land use rights provided by the Transit Cold Storage as mortgage, 13.265 mu was the welfare area of the Transit Cold Storage, i.e., the employee residential area. The land use certificate number for that parcel was Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979.

The Cereals and Oils Company and the Transit Cold Storage failed to perform their repayment obligations. Cinda Xi'an Office filed a lawsuit with the Shaanxi High Court, requesting the court to: order the Cereals and Oils Company to repay the loan principal of RMB 25.6 million and interest of RMB 7,046,315.64 (calculated up to September 20, 2006); order the Transit Cold Storage to bear the security liability for the above principal and interest; order that Cinda Xi'an Office be entitled to priority satisfaction from the proceeds of disposal of the mortgaged property provided by the Transit Cold Storage; and order the Cereals and Oils Company and the Transit Cold Storage to bear the litigation costs.

After trial, the court of first instance held: The Renminbi Loan Contract numbered 2003 Shan Zhong Ying Jie Zi No. 022 signed between the Cereals and Oils Company and BOC Shaanxi Branch, and the Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement signed between BOC Shaanxi Branch and Cinda Xi'an Office, were the true expressions of intent of the parties and did not violate mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and should be valid. The Cereals and Oils Company failed to perform its repayment obligations as agreed under the contract, which constituted a breach of contract and should bear corresponding civil liability in accordance with the law. As for the Mortgage Contract numbered 2003 Shan Zhong Ying Di Zi No. 022 signed between the Transit Cold Storage and BOC Shaanxi Branch, except for the 13.265 mu of land use rights under the Land Use Certificate Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979 provided by the Transit Cold Storage, which was invalid because there was a dispute over those rights, violating Article 37, paragraph 1, item (4) of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China ("Property with unclear ownership or use rights or under dispute shall not be mortgaged"), the remaining part was valid as it complied with Article 34, paragraph 1, item (3) of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China ("State-owned land use rights, buildings, and other fixtures above ground that the mortgagor has the right to dispose of according to law may be mortgaged"). The Transit Cold Storage should, in accordance with the valid part of the mortgage contract, bear the mortgage security liability for the debts owed by the Cereals and Oils Company. As both BOC Shaanxi Branch and the Transit Cold Storage were at fault for the partial invalidity of the mortgage, according to Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China ("Where the main contract is valid but the security contract is invalid, and the creditor is not at fault, the security provider and the debtor shall bear joint and several compensation liability for the economic loss of the creditor under the main contract; where both the creditor and the security provider are at fault, the portion of civil liability to be borne by the security provider shall not exceed one-half of the amount that the debtor cannot repay"), the mortgagor Transit Cold Storage, after the mortgagee Cinda Xi'an Office realizes the mortgage on the valid part of the mortgaged property, shall bear one-half of the compensation liability for the portion of the Cereals and Oils Company's debt that remains unpaid. According to the facts found in this case, the maturity date of the Cereals and Oils Company's loan of RMB 25.6 million was March 16, 2004, and the statute of limitations would expire on March 16, 2006. After Cinda Xi'an Office acquired the creditor's rights, it published collection announcements in the "Shaanxi Daily" on November 10, 2004, and June 18, 2006, asserting its rights against the Cereals and Oils Company. According to Article 10 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Cases Involving the Acquisition, Management, and Disposal of Assets Formed from Non-performing Loans of State-owned Banks by Financial Asset Management Companies ("If the original creditor bank publishes a creditor's rights transfer announcement or notice containing debt collection content in a newspaper with national or provincial influence, such announcement or notice may serve as evidence of interruption of the statute of limitations"), the statute of limitations for this loan was interrupted by Cinda Xi'an Office's assertion of rights. Therefore, the defense of the Cereals and Oils Company that the loan was time-barred could not be sustained. Although this loan was a "new loan to repay old loan," the March 28, 2003 reply from the Xi'an Municipal Bureau of Land Resources and Housing Administration to the Transit Cold Storage regarding "renewal of real estate mortgage registration" proved that the Transit Cold Storage held the loan contract numbered 2003 Shan Zhong Ying Jie Zi No. 022 (the "new loan to repay old loan" contract) signed between the Cereals and Oils Company and BOC Shaanxi Branch, thereby proving that the Transit Cold Storage knew that this loan was a "new loan to repay old loan." Therefore, the Transit Cold Storage's argument that it was unaware of the "new loan to repay old loan" and that the mortgage was invalid and its security liability should be exempted could not be sustained. The reply from the Xi'an Municipal Bureau of Land Resources and Housing Administration regarding the renewal of mortgage registration for the Transit Cold Storage stated that the mortgage term was 12 months from the date of registration. After the term expired, the Transit Cold Storage did not renew the registration. However, according to Article 12, paragraph (1) of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China ("The security period agreed by the parties or required to be registered by the registration authority is not legally binding on the existence of the security interest"), the Transit Cold Storage's defense that the mortgage was invalid because it was not renewed after the mortgage term expired could not be sustained. As for the mortgaged property involved in this case, except for the 13.265 mu of land use rights under Land Use Certificate Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979, which was invalid due to violation of Article 37, paragraph 1, item (4) of the Security Law, the Transit Cold Storage exclusively owned the 31.201 mu of land use rights under Land Use Certificate Xi Wei Guo Yong (2001) Zi No. 299, and there was no issue of co-ownership of the mortgaged property. Therefore, the Transit Cold Storage's defense that the mortgage was invalid because it was not consented by co-owners could not be sustained. Its argument that the statute of limitations had expired also did not conform to the facts and could not be sustained. Although Cinda Xi'an Office's two newspaper announcements did not include the name of the Transit Cold Storage, according to Article 52 of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China ("The mortgage right shall exist simultaneously with the creditor's rights it secures; if the creditor's rights are extinguished, the mortgage right shall also be extinguished"), since the creditor's rights in this case have not been extinguished, Cinda Xi'an Office's mortgage right still exists. In summary, the Transit Cold Storage's arguments that the mortgage guarantee was invalid and requesting exemption from security liability could not be sustained. In accordance with Articles 84, 106(I), 108, and 140 of the General Principles of Civil Law of the People's Republic of China; Article 207 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China; Articles 33, 37(I)(4), 41, 52, 53, and 57 of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China; Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Security Law of the People's Republic of China; and Article 10 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Cases Involving the Acquisition, Management, and Disposal of Assets Formed from Non-performing Loans of State-owned Banks by Financial Asset Management Companies, the court rendered the following judgment:
1. The Renminbi Loan Contract numbered 2003 Shan Zhong Ying Jie Zi No. 022 signed between BOC Shaanxi Branch and the Cereals and Oils Company, and the Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement signed between BOC Shaanxi Branch and Cinda Xi'an Office, are valid; in the Mortgage Contract numbered 2003 Shan Zhong Ying Di Zi No. 022 signed between BOC Shaanxi Branch and the Transit Cold Storage, except that the mortgage of the 13.265 mu of land use rights under Land Use Certificate Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979 is invalid, the remaining part is valid.
2. The Cereals and Oils Company shall, within 10 days after this judgment becomes effective, repay Cinda Xi'an Office the loan principal of RMB 25.6 million and interest (interest within the loan contract term shall be calculated at the interest rate stipulated in the loan contract; interest on the overdue portion shall be calculated at the overdue penalty interest rate for the same period as stipulated by the People's Bank of China until the date of payment).
3. If the Cereals and Oils Company fails to perform the above payment obligations, Cinda Xi'an Office is entitled to be satisfied with priority from the proceeds obtained from discount, auction, or sale of the 31.201 mu of land use rights under Land Use Certificate Xi Wei Guo Yong (2001) Zi No. 299 provided by the Transit Cold Storage as mortgaged property.
4. After the execution of the above payment obligations under items 2 and 3, if Cinda Xi'an Office still has a portion of its creditor's rights unsatisfied, the Transit Cold Storage shall bear one-half of the compensation liability for the portion of the Cereals and Oils Company's debt that cannot be repaid.
5. After the Transit Cold Storage performs its security obligations, it is entitled to recourse against the Cereals and Oils Company.
If the monetary payment obligations are not performed within the period specified in this judgment, the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
Court acceptance fee: RMB 86,621; preservation fee: RMB 81,616, borne by the Cereals and Oils Company.

Cinda Xi'an Office, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Shaanxi High People's Court, appealed to this Court, stating:
(I) The judgment of first instance had unclear findings of fact and insufficient evidence; Cinda Xi'an Office holds a legal mortgage right over the 13.265 mu of land use rights under Land Use Certificate Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979. According to the Security Law, a party may fully mortgage state-owned land use rights under its name. As long as the mortgagee and the mortgagor complete the registration of the mortgaged property with the land administration department, the mortgage right is legally valid. Without evidence to the contrary, a legally valid mortgage right cannot be arbitrarily overturned. The original creditor bank and the Transit Cold Storage entered into a mortgage contract for the land use rights under Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979, and on March 28 of the same year, they completed mortgage registration with the Xi'an Municipal Bureau of Land Resources and Housing Administration, which issued the mortgage approval document Shi Guo Tu Fang Guan Fa (2003) No. 109. Cinda Xi'an Office and the Transit Cold Storage entered into a mortgage contract and completed the mortgage registration procedures in accordance with the law. The actions of both parties fully complied with the Security Law and relevant regulations. Cinda Xi'an Office's mortgage right over the above land use rights is completely legal and valid.
(II) The judgment of first instance erroneously applied the law. The state-owned land use rights under Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979 belong to the Transit Cold Storage, and there is no dispute over the rights. Multiple pieces of evidence submitted by Cinda Xi'an Office are sufficient to prove that the state-owned land use rights under Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979 legally belong to the Transit Cold Storage. The rights to this parcel of land are clear and without any dispute. The Transit Cold Storage is fully entitled to establish a mortgage on it. The finding of the first instance that the above land use rights constitute property with unclear ownership or use rights or under dispute is an error in the application of law.
(III) The court of first instance determined that the land use rights over which the appellant holds a mortgage right were disputed simply because there were previously employee residential buildings on the mortgaged land, which is clearly based on insufficient evidence. The 13.265 mu of land provided by the Transit Cold Storage for mortgage was used, as early as 1992, with the approval of the Shaanxi Provincial Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation Committee and other relevant departments, to construct three employee apartment buildings with a total of 46 units. The property ownership certificates were obtained on May 9, 2001, but the nature of the land remained allocated land. Under these circumstances, the Transit Cold Storage established a mortgage on the land use rights. The first instance judgment found that the land use rights over which Cinda Xi'an Office held a mortgage right were disputed and thus declared the mortgage invalid. This finding cannot stand. The reason is that the "property with unclear use rights or under dispute" referred to in the Security Law only means that there is a dispute between two parties over the use rights, which is being resolved by a judicial or administrative department. In such a situation, because the dispute over the land use rights is being handled by the relevant department, the law does not permit such land use rights to be mortgaged. In this case, the state-owned land use rights under Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979 are recorded in the name of the Transit Cold Storage in the archives, and no unit or individual has ever disputed the land use rights with the Transit Cold Storage. Although the employees of the Transit Cold Storage have built residential houses on the land, this cannot negate the mortgage right that the appellant has registered with the land administration department. Therefore, the first instance judgment that the appellant's mortgage right was partially invalid is clearly based on insufficient evidence. In summary, the first instance judgment had unclear findings of fact, insufficient evidence, and erroneous application of law. The appellant's mortgage right over the state-owned land use rights under Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979 is legally valid. The appellant requests: 1. To reverse items 1, 3, and 4 of the Civil Judgment (2007) Shan Min Er Chu Zi No. 2 of the Shaanxi High People's Court; to amend the judgment and confirm that Cinda Xi'an Office holds mortgage rights over both parcels of land provided by the Transit Cold Storage as mortgage, that the Transit Cold Storage should bear the security liability, and that Cinda Xi'an Office has the right to dispose of the state-owned land use rights under Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979 and Xi Wei Guo Yong (2001) Zi No. 299 held by the Transit Cold Storage and be satisfied with priority from the proceeds of the disposal of the mortgaged property. 2. To order the Cereals and Oils Company and the Transit Cold Storage to bear all litigation costs of this case.

Appellee Xi'an Transit Cold Storage (hereinafter "Transit Cold Storage") argued in its defense: The facts found in the first-instance judgment were clear, the evidence was sufficient, and the law was correctly applied. The judgment should be affirmed, and the appeal of the Xi'an Office of Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Cinda Xi'an Office") should be dismissed. (1) The mortgage over the 13.265 mu of land under Land Use Certificate No. Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979 was invalid. In the first instance, Cinda Xi'an Office did not produce the certificate of he (right in rem). It should bear the legal consequences of failing to meet its burden of proof. The mortgage contract was not consented to by other co-owners, rendering the mortgage invalid. To resolve the issue of employee residential buildings, Transit Cold Storage borrowed funds to construct the buildings on September 8, 1992, with approval from the Provincial Economic and Trade Commission (Document No. (1992) 349), and filed for record with the Provincial Discipline Inspection Commission, the Provincial Construction Bank, the Municipal Planning Bureau, the Municipal Real Estate Bureau, the Municipal Land Bureau, and other relevant authorities. A total of 46 employees obtained property ownership certificates on May 9, 2001, with the property rights defined as private. During the first-instance trial, Cinda Xi'an Office admitted that it had inspected the site when processing the mortgage and knew that there were three employee family-funded collective residential buildings with co-owners. The land mortgage was not consented to by the co-owners, and the mortgage act was invalid. (2) The first-instance judgment correctly applied the law, as the state-owned land under Certificate No. Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979 had serious ownership issues. First, the 46 employees obtained their property certificates before the mortgage was created. On May 9, 2001, the 46 employees obtained property ownership certificates from the Xi'an Real Estate Management Bureau, and these 46 property owners held the right to use the 13.265 mu of land under Certificate No. Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979. Second, there was no national policy regarding the subdivision of state-owned land certificates for employee-funded collective housing and large state-owned land certificates, so Transit Cold Storage could not process such a subdivision. Third, Cinda Xi'an Office knew that the mortgaged land had three employee collective residential buildings and that the employees had obtained legally valid property certificates, yet it disregarded the law and executed the invalid mortgage on March 28, 2003. Even if Cinda Xi'an Office was unaware of the ownership status of the mortgaged property, it could not obtain the mortgage right. (3) Cinda Xi'an Office was seriously at fault in this case and should bear legal liability on its own. When processing the mortgage, the original creditor bank knew that the mortgaged property included three employee collective residential buildings and that 46 employees had property certificates. Knowing that the ownership and use rights of the mortgaged land were unclear, it forcibly executed an invalid mortgage contract. As a professional institution, Cinda Xi'an Office should bear the legal consequences itself. The mortgage registration period expired without renewal, making the mortgage invalid. Cinda Xi'an Office's lawsuit against Transit Cold Storage had exceeded the statute of limitations, and the lawsuit should be dismissed upon adjudication. According to Article 202 of the Property Law of the PRC, "The mortgagor shall exercise the mortgage right within the statute of limitations period of the principal claim; if not exercised, the people's court shall not grant protection." Regarding these two pieces of mortgaged land, Cinda Xi'an Office did not exercise the mortgage right within the statute of limitations period of the principal claim, so the people's court should not protect it. (4) Knowing that the mortgage right was invalid, Cinda Xi'an Office applied to the court to seal the originally mortgaged land. The 46 employees who held property certificates on that land, along with their hundreds of family members, expressed strong dissatisfaction and threatened to file petitions, seriously affecting social stability and harmony.

The original defendant, the Grain and Oil Company (hereinafter "Grain and Oil Company"), stated in its defense: (1) Cinda Xi'an Office's first-instance claims were untenable and lacked support. There was no basis for Cinda Xi'an Office's request for Grain and Oil Company to repay RMB 25.6 million. (2) The mortgage act was invalid, and Transit Cold Storage should not bear guarantee liability. When the loan contract was executed, the original creditor bank already knew that Grain and Oil Company was unable to repay the loan, and seriously violated the relevant provisions of the Commercial Banking Law by allowing Grain and Oil Company to present a blank mortgage contract for Transit Cold Storage to seal. The mortgage contract was filled in by the bank only after the seal was affixed. Transit Cold Storage was completely unaware that this was a loan to replace the old with the new. The original creditor bank never met with Transit Cold Storage to negotiate the contract. Transit Cold Storage is an independent legal person and never authorized Grain and Oil Company. The mortgage was not approved by the co-owners, making it invalid. The mortgage had expired without renewal, and should be deemed invalid. According to Article 202 of the Property Law, since Cinda Xi'an Office did not exercise the mortgage right within the statute of limitations period of the principal claim, it should not be protected. (3) Grain and Oil Company's loans were incurred during the planned economy period to complete foreign exchange indicator tasks assigned by the state, and were essentially policy-related suspended losses. Grain and Oil Company was already insolvent and in bankruptcy proceedings. Cinda Xi'an Office was fully aware of Grain and Oil Company's financial and operational condition, and was seriously at fault in signing the loan contract; it should bear the legal consequences itself.

Upon appeal, this court finds that, in addition to the facts found by the first-instance court, the following facts are established: On the land under Land Use Certificate No. Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979, there are employee residential buildings, among which 46 employees hold "Property Ownership Certificates" issued by the Xi'an Real Estate Management Bureau, with issuance dates partly on May 21, 2001, and partly on May 22, 2001. The floor plan annotations in the property ownership certificates are dated May 9, 2001. Article 5 "Mortgage Property" of the "Mortgage Contract" (No. 2003 Shaan Zhong Ying Di Zi No. 022) signed between Transit Cold Storage and Shaanxi Branch of Bank of China (hereinafter "Shaanxi BOC") stipulates: "The net value of the mortgage property is RMB 41,065,500. For details, see the list of mortgage property." The attached list of mortgage property indicates "Name of mortgage property" as "Land, real estate." The Xi'an Real Estate Management Bureau issued a reply letter (Shi Fang Han [2008] No. 101) on July 18, 2008, stating: "Upon verification, the state-owned land use certificates of Shaanxi Province Grain and Oil Import and Export Company Xi'an Transit Cold Storage, namely Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979 and Xi Wei Guo Yong (2001) Zi No. 299, have undergone mortgage registration procedures at our bureau. The initial registration was on March 6, 2001, and the renewal registration was on March 28, 2003. The designated use for both land certificates is storage land." "Before the 2002 institutional reform, both the Municipal Real Estate Bureau and the Municipal Land Bureau conducted land use right mortgage registration business. When the Municipal Real Estate Bureau processed mortgage registration, it temporarily held the original land use certificate until the mortgage registration was cancelled. After the institutional reform, the two bureaus merged. Following a study by the bureau leadership, the mortgage registration business originally processed by the Real Estate Bureau before the merger was treated as legacy issues, with renewal and cancellation registrations handled by the Property Rights Market Division. According to this decision, after the merger, the mortgage registration business handled by the Market Division was all legacy issues, and copies of the registration filing certificates were sent to the Cadastre and Land Administration Division, the Real Estate Transaction Management Center, and the Housing Property Rights and Registration Management Center. After the 2005 institutional reform, the two bureaus were separated, and these legacy issues continued to be handled by our bureau." "The real estate property registration of Shaanxi Province Grain and Oil Import and Export Company Xi'an Transit Cold Storage totals three locations, of which two are employee residential buildings (Certificates No. 1150112018-15-19 and 1150112018-15-3, which have been divided into individual units through housing reform, with issuance dates of September 1998), and one is an office building (Certificate No. 1150112018-15-2, issuance date September 1998). The land certificates submitted were Wei Guo Yong (95) Zi No. 1321 and No. 1322. None of the three property registrations show any connection to Land Use Certificate No. Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979." In the land registration review form in the land file for Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979 kept by the Xi'an Bureau of Land and Resources, it is indicated that the "declared building ownership" of this parcel of land is "owned by this unit," the "building type" is "single-story buildings, multi-story buildings," the "land use" is "storage," and it also states: "This parcel of land is used by Shaanxi Province Grain and Oil Import and Export Company Xi'an Transit Cold Storage, which holds State-Owned Land Use Certificate No. Wei Guo Yong (1995) Zi No. 1321, with a certified land area of 11.23659 square meters. After a cadastral survey by the Weiyang District Land Bureau, the land area is 13.265 mu, and the use is residential. The originally issued State-Owned Land Use Certificate No. Wei Guo Yong (1995) Zi No. 1321 is cancelled. A new certificate is approved for issuance."

This court holds that the focus of the dispute between the parties in this second instance is the validity of the mortgage over the state-owned land use right under Certificate No. Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979.

Article 31 of the Urban Real Estate Administration Law of the PRC provides: "When real estate is transferred or mortgaged, the ownership of the house and the land use right within the area occupied by the house shall be transferred or mortgaged simultaneously." Article 6 of the Measures for the Administration of Urban House Ownership Registration promulgated by the Ministry of Construction on October 27, 1997, provides: "House ownership registration shall follow the principle that the owner of the house and the holder of the land use right within the area occupied by the house are the same subject." Article 11 of the Interim Measures for the Administration of Allocated Land Use Rights promulgated by the State Land Administration on March 8, 1992, provides: "When land use rights are transferred or mortgaged, the ownership of the above-ground buildings and other attachments shall be transferred or mortgaged simultaneously; when the ownership of above-ground buildings and other attachments is transferred or mortgaged, the land use right within the scope of their use shall be transferred or mortgaged simultaneously, except where the above-ground buildings and other attachments are transferred as chattels." The principle of unity of rights, i.e., "the land follows the house, and the house follows the land," is a consistent principle in China's real property rights. The transferor of a property has the obligation to transfer the land use right within the area occupied by the sold house to the transferee, and the transferee has the right to demand the transfer of the land use right within the area occupied by the purchased house to themselves. Before the registration of the change in land use right is completed, the transferor is the nominal registrant, but the transferee is the substantive rights holder and may request that the land use right be changed to their name.

The Mortgage Contract (No. Shaan Zhong Ying Di Zi No. 022) stipulated that the mortgaged property was "land and real estate." Transit Cold Storage, in 2003, submitted to the Xi'an Municipal Bureau of Land Resources and Housing a document titled "Letter Regarding Consent to Continue Using Land and Ground Buildings for Loan Mortgage." Therefore, although the mortgage registration only covered the state-owned land use right under Certificate No. Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979, it should be deemed that the parties agreed to mortgage the land use right and the ownership of the above-ground buildings simultaneously. However, the ownership of the employee residential buildings among the above-ground buildings had already been transferred to the employee-purchasers, and Transit Cold Storage had no right to dispose of them. According to Article 51 of the Contract Law of the PRC, "Where a person without the right of disposition disposes of another's property, the contract is valid only if the right holder ratifies it or the person without the right of disposition acquires the right of disposition after concluding the contract." This mortgage contract was not ratified by the employee-purchasers who were the owners of the above-ground buildings. Moreover, the Land Use Certificate No. Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979 already indicated that there were above-ground buildings on the parcel and designated them as the welfare zone of Transit Cold Storage. The ownership of the employee residential buildings among the above-ground buildings had been registered and transferred to the employee-purchasers. The original creditor bank failed to ascertain the actual ownership of the above-ground buildings and accepted the mortgage, also at fault. Therefore, the mortgage contract was invalid, and the mortgage right established under this contract was correspondingly invalid.

In this case, although the employee residential buildings did not occupy the entire 13.265 mu of land under Certificate No. Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979, the invalidity of the mortgage right established over this land use right extends to the entire parcel. The mortgage over the state-owned land use right under Certificate No. Xi Wei Guo Yong (2000) Zi No. 979 was invalid. Cinda Xi'an Office's appeal argument that it held a mortgage right over the above state-owned land use right cannot be sustained and is not adopted by this court. The first-instance judgment correctly found that both Shaanxi BOC and Transit Cold Storage were at fault for the invalidity of this part of the mortgage, and that Transit Cold Storage should bear partial compensation liability for the portion of Grain and Oil Company's debts that remained unsatisfied after Cinda Xi'an Office realized the mortgage over the valid part. However, the first-instance court's determination that Transit Cold Storage should bear one-third of the compensation liability was too low. Although Shaanxi BOC was at fault for the invalidity of the mortgage over the above state-owned land use right, Transit Cold Storage's unauthorized disposition was the primary cause of the invalidity. Therefore, this court adjusts Transit Cold Storage's compensation liability ratio to one-half.

In summary, except for the low ratio of compensation liability assigned to Transit Cold Storage, the other parts of the first-instance judgment are correct and should be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this court hereby orders as follows:

1. Uphold Items 1, 2, 3, and 5 of the Civil Judgment (No. (2007) Shaan Min Er Chu Zi No. 2) of the Shaanxi High People's Court;

2. Amend Item 4 of the above judgment's main text to read: "After the payment obligations in Items 2 and 3 above are executed, if the Xi'an Office of China Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd. still has part of its claims unsatisfied, the Xi'an Transit Cold Storage of Shaanxi Province Grain and Oil Import and Export Company shall bear one-half of the compensation liability for the portion that Shaanxi Province Grain and Oil Import and Export Company cannot satisfy."

The first-instance case acceptance fee and preservation fee shall be executed according to the first-instance judgment. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 102,515.79 shall be borne by the appellant, Xi'an Office of Cinda Asset Management Co., Ltd., in the amount of RMB 68,343.86, and by the appellee, Xi'an Transit Cold Storage of Shaanxi Province Grain and Oil Import and Export Company, in the amount of RMB 34,171.93.

This judgment is final.
